authority.self_declared_rules_weight: The sheet's own header states: 'Anything which can logically be inferred from these examples is tantamount to a rule unless it is explicitly covered in the written rules.' The examples are therefore a printed rules authority for this edition, not mere illustration.

source.render: embedded page image extracted at native resolution via naw_render.page_image(dpi=400), then rotated -90 degrees to upright; working file C:\VassalNaW\pages\ed2_p02_rot.png at 2550x3300

method.primary: by-eye reading off zoomed crops that were actually opened as images (zoom factors 1.5x to 3.4x of the 2550x3300 upright render)
method.cross_check: Tesseract 5 OCR, multi-PSM, run per tile and positionally mapped back to page fractions (naw_examples.py odds)
method.ocr_status: OCR located and read 12 of the 27 odds labels. Every one of those 12 agreed exactly with the by-eye reading. OCR produced ZERO readings that contradicted the eye, and produced no odds value that the eye had not already read. The other 15 labels were not resolved by OCR at all (the labels are small, isolated, widely letter-spaced serif text on white) and are by-eye only. Per PREP-4's lesson OCR is treated as corroboration, never as authority.
method.circle_tracing: Each printed Battle-situation is delimited by a light grey drawn circle. Membership of each circle was determined by opening the crop and following the drawn line, then checked against the printed odds label. Where two readings of a circle were geometrically possible, the printed odds label discriminated between them; those cases are marked in per-row notes.

header_text_verbatim:
EXAMPLES OF ATTACKS

In the following examples, the Grey units are the Attackers and the untinted units are the Defenders. A circle is drawn around those units (Attacker and Defender) which are involved in combat with each other. Each circled Battle-situation constitutes an attack and would require the rolling of the die. Note than when several attacking and defending units are adjacent to each other the attacks may be constituted in more than one way. Artillery attacks are indicated with an arrow when the defending unit being bombarded is not directly adjacent. The odds of each attack are given next to each situation. Anything which can logically be inferred from these examples is tantamount to a rule unless it is explicitly covered in the written rules.
header_text_notes: Transcribed verbatim from crop a_01_intro.png. The printed text reads 'Note than when several attacking...' - 'than' where the sense requires 'that'. This is what the folio prints; it is NOT normalised here. Flagged because RULEBOOK_VERIFIED.md was found by PREP-4 to have silently normalised a different printed typo ('expends' for the folio's 'extends').

symbol_key_as_read.tint: Grey-filled counter = attacker. Untinted (white) counter = defender. Stated by the header text and consistent across all 27 examples.
symbol_key_as_read.nationality: NOT shown. The examples sheet prints attacker/defender tint instead of the game's national colours (French blue / British red / Prussian green). No example on this page identifies a nationality, so no example constrains which side may perform which attack.
symbol_key_as_read.factors: Two numbers printed as 'C-M': left = Combat Strength, right = Movement Allowance (per RULEBOOK_VERIFIED.md section 3, matching the counter photograph read in PREP-4).

unit_types.artillery: rectangle with a centred filled dot

symbol_key_as_read.echelon: every counter on this sheet carries the XX (division) echelon symbol
symbol_key_as_read.town_hex: drawn as solid black building blocks inside the hex; appears in exactly two examples (EX-03, EX-04) and nowhere else on the sheet
symbol_key_as_read.bombardment: a dashed arrow from the artillery counter to the target hex, drawn only where the target is not adjacent (per the header text)

corpus_summary.prep1_estimate_was: ~24 (index estimate in RULEBOOK_VERIFIED.md section 2); the exact count read here is 27
corpus_summary.note_on_results: The sheet prints odds ONLY. Not one example states a die roll or a Combat Results Table outcome. This corpus therefore validates the ODDS COMPUTATION (strength totals, terrain doubling, rounding, who may combine with whom) and NOT the CRT lookup. A separate validation source is required for the CRT itself.
corpus_summary.column_coverage: The printed CRT has columns 1-5,1-4,1-3,1-2,1-1,2-1,3-1,4-1,5-1,6-1. The examples exercise 1-4, 1-2, 1-1, 2-1, 3-1, 4-1. Columns 1-5, 1-3, 5-1 and 6-1 are NOT exercised by any example, and neither clamp ('worse than 1 to 5' / 'greater than 6 to 1') is demonstrated.

rules_exercised: Ratio rounding in favour of the defender - exercised 10 times with a non-integral raw ratio (EX-05 8:3, EX-06 9:4, EX-10 6:4, EX-12 13:4, EX-13 2:3, EX-14 13:6, EX-15 8:3, EX-20 6:4, EX-22 4:3, EX-25 3:2).
Defender in a Town-hex doubles its Combat Strength (EX-04, explicitly annotated 'Doubled due to Town-hex').
Attacker in a Town-hex is NOT doubled (EX-03, same 6 vs 6 units, printed 1 to 1).
Several attackers combine against one defender (EX-06, EX-11, EX-12, EX-15, EX-19, EX-25, EX-27, EX-05).
One attacker attacks several adjacent defenders as one combined defence total (EX-08, EX-26).
Several attackers against several defenders in one attack (EX-14).
Artillery adjacent to its target attacks normally (EX-01).
Artillery bombards a target exactly two hexes away across an empty intervening hex (EX-02, EX-17).
Bombarding artillery strength ADDS to an adjacent attacker's strength in a single combined attack (EX-09, EX-24).
Deliberate low-odds attack (EX-16 at 1 to 4, EX-13/EX-18/EX-21 at 1 to 2, EX-04 at 1 to 2).

Two complete, mutually exclusive, legal partitions of the SAME board position (EX-10/EX-11 vs EX-12/EX-13; and EX-15..EX-21 vs EX-22..EX-27) - the printed demonstration of the header's 'the attacks may be constituted in more than one way'.

Both partitions of the 16-unit battle line attack every defender and use every attacker exactly once, and no unit appears in two attacks - a printed demonstration of the 'all adjacent enemy units must be attacked / all adjacent friendly units must participate / no unit twice' cluster.

battle_line_layout.applies_to: EX-15..EX-21 (PARTITION A) and EX-22..EX-27 (PARTITION B) - the same sixteen-unit position drawn twice
battle_line_layout.adjacency_as_drawn: rows are offset half a hex; row C is offset to the right relative to row B, so C(n) is adjacent to B(n+1) and B(n+2). Row A sits above row B with the same offset sense. Read off the drawing, not inferred from a grid model.
battle_line_layout.structural_property: in BOTH partitions every one of the 9 grey units participates in exactly one attack and every one of the 7 untinted units is attacked exactly once. Nothing is left out, nothing is used twice.

rounding_rule_as_evidenced.printed_wording: the folio's Combat case states the ratio is 'rounded off in favour of the defender' (RULEBOOK_VERIFIED.md section 3); the sheet itself prints no rounding wording
rounding_rule_as_evidenced.behaviour_the_27_examples_are_consistent: if attacker_total >= defender_total: column = floor(attacker_total / defender_total) to 1; else: column = 1 to ceil(defender_total / attacker_total)
rounding_rule_as_evidenced.verification: all 27 rows reproduce their printed odds under this single expression; 10 of them have a non-integral raw ratio and so actually exercise the rounding
rounding_rule_as_evidenced.coverage_gap: EX-13 (2 vs 3, printed 1 to 2) is the ONLY example with a non-integral ratio BELOW 1. It is therefore the sole printed evidence that the defender-favouring direction on the adverse side is ceil rather than floor. A single witness - treat accordingly.
rounding_rule_as_evidenced.status: this expression is OURS, derived from the printed odds; it is not a printed formula. It is offered as the hypothesis the corpus tests, not as a citation.

consistency_with_recorded_rules.checked_against: literature/napoleon-at-waterloo/RULEBOOK_VERIFIED.md section 3 (2nd Edition, printed CRT and TEC)
agreements: 'rounded off in favour of the defender' - all 9 non-integral raw ratios round toward the defender in every example. No counter-example.

printed TEC 'Defending unit DOUBLES its Combat Strength ... Combat Strength remains at normal value when units attack from such terrain' - EX-03 and EX-04 demonstrate both halves with identical units.
'Multiple attackers may combine against one defender; one attacker may attack several adjacent defenders as a single combined defence total' - EX-06/EX-11/EX-15 etc. and EX-08/EX-26 respectively.
'Combat Strength is indivisible' - no example splits a unit's strength across two attacks.
'No defending unit may be attacked more than once per turn; no attacking unit may attack more than once per turn' - both battle-line partitions obey this exactly.
'Deliberate low-odds attacks are explicitly permitted' - EX-16 (1 to 4), EX-13/EX-18/EX-21 (1 to 2).
'Bombarding artillery may attack only a single hex' - every bombardment on the sheet targets exactly one hex.
artillery range 2 - both bombardment distances drawn are exactly two hexes.
consistency_with_recorded_rules.disagreements_note: NONE. Every stated odds ratio on this sheet is reproduced by the rules as recorded in RULEBOOK_VERIFIED.md section 3. Nothing here contradicts the recorded CRT columns, the clamping footnote, the rounding rule, or the Terrain Effects Chart.

questions_the_examples_do_NOT_settle: D4 (TEC vs rules text on Woods/Road doubling) is UNTOUCHED. The only doubling example on the sheet is a Town-hex. No Woods hex, no Woods/Road hex and no road appears anywhere on this page. The worked examples cannot be used to adjudicate D4 either way.

D9 (2nd Ed bombardment while adjacent to a different enemy) is UNTOUCHED. In all four bombardment examples the bombarding artillery has no enemy unit adjacent to it, so the sheet neither confirms nor contradicts the 3rd Edition [5.6] 'not in an enemy ZOC' restriction.
The CRT itself is untouched: no example states a die roll or a result code. AE / Ar / EX / Dr / DE remain validated only by the printed table, not by any worked example.
The clamp footnote ('worse than 1 to 5 treated as 1 to 5; greater than 6 to 1 treated as 6 to 1') is not demonstrated. The most extreme printed odds are 1 to 4 and 4 to 1.
CRT columns 1-5, 1-3, 5-1 and 6-1 are not exercised by any example.
Zones of Control are not drawn or annotated anywhere on the sheet.
Nationality is not shown (attacker/defender is coded by grey tint, not by the game's blue/red/green), so no example constrains which side performs which attack.
Terrain is not stated for any hex other than the two Town-hexes; the remaining hexes are drawn blank and the sheet does not name them as clear.
unreadable_note: Nothing on page 2 was left unread. All 27 odds labels, the three 'Artillery Attack' annotations, the one 'Doubled due to Town-hex' annotation, every counter's factors and type symbol, and the full header paragraph were resolved at the render resolution used. The count of 27 is a complete enumeration of the circled Battle-situations on the page.
confidence_statement: 27 of 27 examples are 'high' confidence. 12 of the 27 odds labels are independently OCR-confirmed with position; the remaining 15 are by-eye off crops that were actually opened as images at 1.5x-3.4x. OCR contradicted the eye on nothing. The one example whose circle membership was not visually obvious on first pass (EX-26) was re-cropped at 3.4x and re-read before being accepted.
handed_forward: These 27 rows are the validation corpus hard rule #1 requires for the ODDS COMPUTATION of the 2nd Edition. Every one must come out of our odds function with the printed ratio before any combat enforcement ships.
The battle_line_layout block is directly usable as two full-board legality tests: both partitions must be accepted by the gate, and the 'every unit exactly once' property must hold.
EX-03/EX-04 are the terrain-doubling regression pair. EX-05 is the rounding-toward-defender pair-mate. EX-09/EX-24 are the combined-bombardment tests.
A separate source is still needed to validate the CRT lookup itself - no printed 2nd Edition example gives a die roll or a result.
The 3rd Edition's own Examples of Attacks (that PDF's p.11) remain unread by this job, by instruction. If the two editions ever share a combat implementation they must be compared.
